main_text.p: In secundo situ, si terra in Axe quidem, sed non in medio mundi locata esset, hæc sequerentur absurda.

I. In omni climate planum Horizontis secaret cœlum in duas æquales partes, exceptis locis habentibus sphæram rectam. Ergo & zodiacus diuideretur in duos æquales arcus, & sic alicubi plus, alicubi minus sex signis de zodiaco conspiceretur supra Horizontem, quod est contra omnem experientiam.

II. Vmbræ Æquinoctiales Orientis et Occidetis solis non congruerent, ita ut in una recta linea seu ἐπ' εὐθείας consisterent. Nec umbra orientis solis die solstitiali, rectam lineam constitueret cum umbra Solis occidentis die brumali & econuerso.
In tertio situ, Si neq; in axe mundi sita esset, ne-que

page.notes: Engraving of an armillary sphere with zodiac signs and sun/star markings, centre of the page; not transcribed. Roman numerals I. and II. are paragraph numbers, not headings. Greek phrase "ἐπ' εὐθείας" reproduced from the scan as best read; the printed Greek is "ἐπ' εὐθείας" with a leading "ξ" word-break mark, uncertain. Lower page is damaged by staining; the word "que" catchword is read from the foot right.
